A Snapshot of Your Day

Join us as a Regional Commodity Manager and become a vital procurement partner for business stakeholders across Northern Europe, focusing primarily on the Danish market. In this dynamic role, you will lead the implementation of procurement strategies, governance, and sourcing initiatives while managing supplier relationships. You will collaborate closely with the Indirect Materials organization, identifying commercial opportunities and contributing to sourcing strategies that drive value through supplier optimization and cost improvements. Engage with regional procurement teams, global commodity managers, and suppliers to enhance procurement performance and create a sustainable business impact.

How You’ll Make an Impact

• Drive regional procurement initiatives and implement global sourcing strategies across Northern Europe, particularly in Denmark.

• Develop and execute sourcing, tendering, negotiation, and contract management activities.

• Analyze spending, supplier, and market data to uncover savings opportunities and optimize supplier portfolios.

• Collaborate with internal stakeholders, suppliers, and our Business Process Outsourcing (BPO) partner to ensure supply continuity and support business objectives.

• Promote procurement governance and compliance while monitoring supplier performance and driving continuous improvement initiatives.

What You Bring

• A Master’s degree in Business Administration, Engineering, Supply Chain Management, Procurement, or a related field.

• Several years of experience in procurement, category management, or strategic sourcing within an international and matrix-based organization.

• Strong analytical, negotiation, and stakeholder management skills, with a balance of strategic thinking and pragmatic execution.

• Experience in indirect materials procurement and supplier management, with knowledge of procurement governance and buying channel strategies.

• Fluent English skills are required; additional Nordic language skills are a plus.

About the Team

You will be part of Siemens Energy’s Procurement organization, joining a collaborative team focused on indirect materials. This role offers a unique opportunity to bridge regional procurement leadership and commodity management. You will enhance stakeholder engagement while supporting the development and implementation of category strategies within Office & Factory Supplies. Together with colleagues across Procurement and our BPO partner, you will contribute to Siemens Energy’s procurement transformation, driving standardization, digitalization, and sustainable value creation.

Who is Siemens Gamesa?

Siemens Gamesa is part of Siemens Energy, a global leader in energy technology with a rich legacy of innovation spanning over 150 years. Together, we are committed to making sustainable, reliable, and affordable energy a reality by pushing the boundaries of what is possible. As a leading player in the wind industry and manufacturer of wind turbines, we are passionate about driving the energy transition and providing innovative solutions that meet the growing energy demand of the global community.

At Siemens Gamesa, we are constantly seeking talented individuals to join our team and support our focus on energy transformation.

Find out how you can make a difference at Siemens Gamesa: https://www.siemens-energy.com/global/en/home/careers/working-with-us.html

Our Commitment to Diversity

Lucky for us, we are not all the same. Through diversity, we generate power. We run on inclusion and our combined creative energy is fueled by over 130 nationalities. Siemens Energy celebrates character – no matter what ethnic background, gender, age, religion, identity, or disability. We energize society, all of society, and we do not discriminate based on our differences.

Rewards/Benefits

Here are examples of the rewards and benefits Siemens Energy offers:

• Opportunities to work with a global team

• Opportunities to work on and lead a variety of innovative projects

• Medical benefits

• Remote/Flexible work

• Time off/Paid holidays and parental leave

• Continual learning through the Learn@Siemens-Energy platform

• Access to a variety of employee resource groups

Application

Don’t hesitate to apply before the 10th November 2026. Ongoing selection is applied; the role might be filled before the last application date.

_Do you want to join a global leader in renewable energy infrastructure? If so, CIP Fund Solutions (CIP FS) is looking for an AI Business Manager to join our Digital Development team.

**Team

**The AI team is a cross-functional team dedicated to embedding AI directly into CIP's business lifecycles and day-to-day operations across the platform and sits within the wider Digital Development team.

**Role

**The AI Business Manager is responsible for ensuring AI creates measurable business value across CIP's business lifecycles and works directly with lifecycle owners, product teams, delivery teams, and business stakeholders to identify opportunities, prioritize initiatives, drive adoption, and embed AI capabilities into day-to-day processes and ways of working.

The AI Business Manager serves as the bridge between business priorities and AI capabilities, ensuring that AI is integrated directly into the Investor, Investment, Fund & Investment Management, and Project lifecycles rather than delivered as standalone technology initiatives. The role is accountable for helping lifecycle teams identify where AI can accelerate outcomes, improve decision-making, increase productivity, and enhance user experiences while ensuring appropriate governance and value realization.

**Responsibilities will consist of, but are not limited to:

**Lifecycle Partnership and Business Engagement

• Partner with lifecycle owners and business stakeholders to understand priorities and strategic objectives, identifying where AI can improve outcomes, efficiency, and decision quality.

• Participate in lifecycle planning and roadmap discussions to embed AI initiatives into business plans from the outset, acting as the primary AI partner for assigned lifecycle domains.

AI Opportunity and Use Case Management

• Facilitate identification, assessment, and prioritization of AI use cases, maintaining the opportunity pipeline based on business value, feasibility, and strategic alignment.

• Develop business cases, value hypotheses, and success metrics, supporting initiatives from ideation and validation through deployment and value realization.

Embedding AI into Business Lifecycles

• Work with business and technology teams to integrate AI into core processes, products, and workflows, redesigning ways of working where relevant and driving adoption of AI-powered tools.

• Support the evolution of lifecycle operating models to treat AI as a native capability, scaling effective patterns across domains.

Governance and Responsible AI

• Ensure AI initiatives comply with governance, security, risk, privacy, and regulatory requirements, coordinating with legal, risk, compliance, and information security stakeholders as needed.

• Support lifecycle teams in navigating AI policies and approval processes, promoting responsible AI practices and appropriate human oversight.

Value Realization and Performance Management

• Track KPIs for AI adoption, utilization, and business value, measuring realized benefits such as productivity gains, cost savings, and risk reduction.

• Provide regular updates to leadership on AI portfolio performance and lifecycle impact.

Change, Communication, and Enablement

• Manage efforts for stakeholder engagement, communications, and change management for AI initiatives, supporting training and capability-building across lifecycle teams.

• Build and maintain networks of AI champions and subject matter experts, promoting a culture of experimentation and responsible AI usage.

**You

**You have a relevant educational background within business, data science, technology, or a similar field. In addition, you have a good understanding of business processes, operating models, and digital transformation, and 5+ years of experience working with technology transformation, AI, data, automation, or similar initiatives, with the ability to translate business challenges into practical AI opportunities and outcomes.

We look for the following in a candidate:

• Good stakeholder management and communication skills, comfortable translating between business and technology audiences to turn emerging AI capabilities into practical business value.

• Experience driving change, adoption, and organizational enablement initiatives.

• Ability to manage multiple initiatives and priorities in a dynamic environment.

• Curious, business-oriented, and outcome-focused.

• Combines strategic thinking with hands-on execution and is motivated by delivering measurable impact through technology-enabled change.

**The process

**Please apply online as soon as possible as applications will be processed on an ongoing basis. For questions related to the role, please reach out to our Talent Acquisition team at recruitment@cipfs.com. We do not include CV's and Cover Letters sent by email.

As we continue to improve our candidate experience, diversity and avoid unconscious bias, please avoid having a photo in your CV. We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality for all applicants.

Please be aware that we will not accept speculative CV submissions for any of our roles from recruitment agencies, and any unsolicited candidate submissions will be exempt from any payment expectations and ownership.

---

**CIP Fund Solutions’ commitment to diversity and inclusion

**CIP Fund Solutions is committed to securing a diverse and inclusive work environment where everyone feels respected and heard.

A diverse workforce allows CIP Fund Solutions to achieve results through different approaches and solutions to task execution and problem solving. We want all our employees to have equal opportunities for personal growth and career opportunities regardless of age, gender, sexual orientation, disability, religion, nationality, or ethnicity.

**CIP Fund Solutions

**CIP FS’ purpose is to enable CIP’s ambition to scale rapidly over the coming strategy-period - supporting our colleagues with professional and efficient financial, legal, tax and business operations through the cycle from fund formation and capital raising, to deploying investments into construction of large-scale greenfield renewable energy assets, as well as M&A.

For more information, please visit CIP Fund Solutions.

As Adv Utilities Professional, you will keep the utility systems in building DF running reliably, so production can run with minimal stops. You will own the daily operation, maintenance and development of these systems, and make sure the building and utilities meet GMP requirements, including in audits and authority inspections. Your work supports a stable, compliant production environment, so medicines can reach people living with serious chronic diseases.

What you’ll bring

You combine technical depth with a structured way of working, and you can turn complex technical and regulatory content into clear, usable documentation.

• An engineering degree or a similar technical education. Other academic backgrounds are relevant if you can show strong skills in technical or regulatory documentation.

• Hands-on experience with HVAC, cooling, heating, steam, compressed air or vacuum systems, and with BMS, FMS and CTS systems.

• Experience with documentation, quality, validation or technical support in a GMP-regulated setting.

• Strong written communication: you are precise, correct and professional, and you structure and review documents, so they are easy to use in practice.

• Working knowledge of GMP and ISO 9001 as they apply to daily tasks, and knowledge of CE marking.

• Good collaboration skills in a broad network of stakeholders.

• Experience with structured problem solving such as KATA and A3, or with water systems, calibration, room qualification and validation.

What you’ll do

You will be the process responsible for the operation and maintenance of the utility systems in building DF and the PS Warehouse, and the person colleagues turn to when something needs to be fixed, documented or decided.

• Operate, maintain and optimise utility systems such as HVAC, cooling, heating, steam, compressed air and vacuum, including technical upkeep that keeps unplanned stops to a minimum.

• Make the most of our FMS, CTS and BMS systems for monitoring buildings and room conditions and keep developing how they are used.

• Keep the building and utilities GMP-compliant, from validation and risk assessments to non-conformances, change requests and quality indicators.

• Write, update and review SOPs, service cards, maintenance instructions, machine documentation and validation documents in clear, precise language, and train colleagues in practice.

• Present your own area in audits and authority inspections, and handle urgent utility issues, escalating when needed.

• Drive and support structured problem solving, improvement work and projects such as rebuilds and new purchases, and plan and prioritise your own tasks.

Who you’ll work with

You will join the Facility Management team within Global Manufacturing & Supply, where colleagues work across the value chain to keep production running for the people who need our medicines. You will work closely with your team and with technicians, production departments and technical partners in building DF and the PS Warehouse, a site with a large network of stakeholders.

Externally, you will collaborate with facility management providers, the energy supplier in Kalundborg, the Hallas Park landowners’ association and Kalundborg Fire and Rescue Service, as well as other suppliers and Novo Nordisk colleagues. You will agree priorities for the building and shared utilities with production areas, and move between daily operations and cross-organisational coordination. The work is based in Denmark.

What you can expect here

You will work in a complex, GMP-regulated environment where your expertise is valued and your voice is heard. Strong written and technical skills matter here, and the role offers room to build the rest: you will be supported with on-the-job learning, relevant training and close collaboration with experienced colleagues. You are trusted to take ownership, and you will be part of a team that acts with clarity, speed and care for quality.

What we offer

At Novo, you’ll join a global healthcare company with a unique culture and strong results. We offer continuous learning, career development, and benefits tailored to your life and career stage.

Salary:  For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from 570,200.00 to 838,100.00 DKK, corresponding to the level of the position.

The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge, and relevant experience.

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area and relevant market benchmarks.

Learn more about our Reward Philosophy here.

Start now

Your impact begins today. If you are ready to keep critical utility systems stable, compliant and well documented, apply for the Adv Utilities Professional role by 6 November 2026. We review applications on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

For further information, please contact Carsten Joachim Hansen, Senior manager CJHH@novonordisk.com

We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality of opportunity for all our job applicants.

Do you enjoy handling all kinds of user’s questions related to computers? Are you passionate about IT support? If both answers are yes, we can offer you a challenging position, great colleagues and the opportunity to combine your education with hand-on experience in a global company.

To work at DHI means being part of an organization that is the global leader in solving the world’s toughest challenges in water environments. We will offer you:

Office location

Hørsholm, Denmark - 25 km north of Copenhagen.

Application / next step

There is no deadline, but we will hold interviews on ongoing basis. We are aiming to find the right candidate as soon as possible.

DHI are the first people you should call when you have a tough challenge to solve in a water environment – be it a river, a reservoir, an ocean, a coastline, within a city or a factory.

Our knowledge of water environments is second-to-none. It represents 50 years of dedicated research and real-life experience from more than 140 countries. We strive to make this knowledge globally accessible to clients and partners by channelling it through our local teams and unique software.

Our world is water. So whether you need to save water, share it fairly, improve its quality, quantify its impact or manage its flow, we can help. Our knowledge, combined with our team's expertise and the power of our technology, holds the key to unlocking the right solution.

Join us in this role where you’ll act as the accounting lead on some of the world’s largest and most complex renewable energy transactions. Your IFRS expertise will help shape transaction structures and inform key investment decisions. You’ll assess the accounting implications of complex M&A transactions, advise on proposed structures, and translate your conclusions into clear insights that support commercial decisions.

**Welcome to IC Projects & IFRS

**You’ll be part of IC Projects & IFRS where you will act as the accounting lead on M&A transactions including acquisitions, divestments, farm-downs, joint ventures, and strategic partnerships. You’ll join a highly specialised team of eight accounting professionals and work closely with our Partnerships and M&A organisation, external advisers, auditors, and a team of around 40 M&A professionals who originate and execute transactions across Europe, North America, and Asia-Pacific. In this role, you’ll support complex international transactions and help ensure high-quality accounting decisions across the Group.

As a team, we share knowledge, explore complex accounting questions together, and support one another in delivering high-quality advice. We value different perspectives, open dialogue, flexibility, and a healthy work-life balance.

**You’ll play an important role in:

**

• acting as the IFRS accounting lead on acquisitions, divestments, farm-downs, joint ventures, structured financing arrangements, and strategic partnerships

• assessing accounting implications early in the transaction process and advising on proposed deal and investment structures

• preparing clear IFRS accounting assessments and technical memos that support commercial and management decisions

• reviewing draft contracts, term sheets, bid materials, and other transaction documentation from an accounting perspective

• participating in meetings with investors, external advisers, auditors, and internal stakeholders on transaction-related accounting matters

• contributing to wider Group Finance activities, including financial reporting, accounting policy development, and strategic accounting projects.

**To succeed in the role, you:

**

• bring deep IFRS expertise gained through technical accounting, IFRS advisory or a similar specialist environment

• have experience advising on the IFRS implications of M&A transactions within a listed company, international group, professional services firm, or a comparable organisation

• can translate complex accounting matters into clear, practical conclusions for management, commercial colleagues, and other non-accounting stakeholders

• build strong working relationships and communicate confidently across finance, Partnerships & M&A, management, external advisers, and auditors

• approach complex assignments analytically and systematically, take ownership of your work, and remain adaptable to changing transaction priorities

• hold a master’s degree in accounting, auditing, or a related discipline.

Maybe you’ve read the above and can see you have some transferable skills, even though they don’t quite match all the points. If you think you can bring something to the team, we still encourage you to apply.

**Shape the future with us

**Send your application to us as soon as possible. We’ll be conducting interviews on a continuous basis and reserve the right to take down the advert when we’ve found the right candidate.

As an applicant or employee, you may request reasonable work and position accommodation or adjustments via accommodation@orsted.com.

Please note that for your application to be taken into consideration, you must submit your application via our online career pages and answer the screening questions relevant for your country. We don't take applications or inquiries from external recruiters or agencies into account for this position.

**Position salary range:

**For this position, the expected base pay range is kr64,720.00- kr116,496.00 for the advertised location. The offered base salary will be determined within this range based on relevant skills, experience, and expected role fulfilment within the stated pay range to ensure a fair and competitive offer. Where applicable, you may also be eligible for variable payment and a comprehensive benefits package.

**Our benefits package:

**For this position, employees who meet eligibility requirements have access to: employer‑paid pension (11% contribution), full insurance coverage (accident, life, critical illness, and health insurance); five weeks of paid holiday plus 10 additional paid days off per holiday year; a 3% holiday allowance; access to Ørsted Life & Fitness Vitality including fitness classes, physiotherapy, massage, and wellbeing programmes; a multimedia package (mobile phone, PC, internet); staff club membership with sport and cultural activities; and access to the company canteen (monthly lunch scheme or daily tickets).

**About Flatpay

As a Data Engineer in the Marketing team at Flatpay, you’ll collaborate closely with marketers, BI engineers, and analysts to turn business needs into scalable data solutions. You’ll help build and evolve event-driven ETL/ELT pipelines for lead intake, routing, and enrichment, as well as the data platform that powers marketing insights.

What you'll do

• 
Design, build, and operate lead flow pipelines, including monitoring and alerting to ensure reliability

• 
Contribute to the development of internal tools and frameworks for marketing data ingestion and transformation

• 
Enable self-service analytics by structuring clean, well-documented datasets for dashboards and reporting tools

• 
Partner with marketing analysts and stakeholders to translate business needs into robust data solutions

• 
Build and maintain data models that support campaign performance tracking, attribution, and customer segmentation

Who you are

You are a pragmatic and detail-oriented problem solver who enjoys building data systems that directly impact business growth. You’re comfortable working cross-functionally with marketers, analysts, and engineers, and you can communicate technical concepts clearly to non-technical stakeholders.

Must-haves

• 
0–3 years of experience as a Data Engineer or similar role

• 
Solid understanding of ETL/ELT design and data modeling principles

• 
Strong Python and SQL skills in production environments

• 
Exposure to cloud infrastructure (Azure, AWS, or GCP)

• 
Strong attention to data quality and consistency

Nice-to-haves

• 
Experience with marketing data and attribution models

• 
Experience with CI/CD workflows, version control (e.g., Git), and testing best practices

• 
Familiarity with data orchestration tools (e.g., Airflow, Prefect, Azure Data Factory)

• 
Experience with modern data platforms (e.g., Databricks, Snowflake, BigQuery)

We’d still love to hear from you if… You don’t check every box but you’re a Python- and SQL-savvy problem solver who’s excited about working with marketing data and enabling growth through better insights. If you’re curious, collaborative, and motivated by building data systems that directly impact business performance, we encourage you to apply!

With us, you’ll experience an ambitious drive to constantly push boundaries and redefine what's possible. While we don’t take ourselves too seriously, we take our responsibility towards our people very seriously. We welcome driven, low-ego individuals who live our values and want to grow with us.

Global Wind Service is looking for a Lean Specialist with strong WTG construction and site management experience to improve planning, productivity and project execution across our global project portfolio.

This is a site-focused role. We are looking for someone who understands how wind turbine construction projects operate in practice, ideally from a Site Manager, Construction Manager, Installation Manager, Supervisor or similar background. WTG construction experience is essential; manufacturing or factory-based experience alone will not meet the requirements of this role.

You will combine your practical site experience with Lean and continuous improvement methods to identify better ways of working and support project teams in implementing them.

The role includes approximately 75–100 days of international travel per year. On site, you will work directly with technicians, supervisors and project teams to understand operational challenges and identify practical improvements. Between visits, you will analyse findings, develop solutions and tools, coach colleagues and follow up on implementation.

Supporting our 1,500 field-based colleagues, your focus will be on improvements that deliver better productivity, consistency and project execution while maintaining safety, quality and compliance with OEM and customer requirements.

Reporting to the Head of Lean@Site, you will join a dedicated team focused on improving site execution, standardising processes and driving continuous improvement.

Locations can be NL, DK & PL.

Role & Responsibilities

• Visit WTG construction sites to identify opportunities to improve productivity, workflow and project execution.

• Identify, quantify and implement practical improvements across wind projects.

• Work closely with Site Managers, Supervisors, technicians and project teams to understand operational challenges and develop workable solutions.

• Apply Lean and continuous improvement methods to planning, workflow, standard work and site execution.

• Coach site leaders and Lean Champions in practical planning, problem-solving and visual management.

• Build strong relationships with project teams and support the adoption of improved ways of working.

• Support site digitalisation initiatives.

• Analyse findings between site visits, develop improvement proposals and coordinate implementation.

• Promote continuous improvement across GWS sites and teams.

Job Requirements

• 3+ years of hands-on experience in WTG construction, installation or site management within the wind industry.

• Strong practical understanding of wind turbine construction and site execution.

• Experience working directly with WTG installation/construction teams and site-based operations.

• Demonstrated ability to identify operational challenges and implement practical improvements.

• Lean, operational excellence or continuous improvement experience is highly valued, but WTG construction experience is the primary requirement.

• Relevant technical, engineering, construction or project management background.

• Formal Lean qualification is an advantage, but not essential.

• Strong communication skills and ability to engage technicians, site management and project teams.

• Structured, analytical and self-driven approach.

• Offshore Pre-Installation experience is an advantage.

• Fluent English, written and spoken.

• Ability to travel internationally 75–100 days per year**.

What We Offer

• Work on high-impact offshore and onshore wind projects with global teams.

• A role with significant site exposure and the opportunity to influence project execution across GWS.

• A dynamic, inclusive and informal work culture.

• Hybrid working and flexibility when not travelling.

• Competitive compensation package including pension, insurance, laptop and mobile.

Ready to improve how wind projects are delivered? Apply now and bring your WTG construction and site experience where it matters.

We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality of opportunity for all our job applicants.

jobs.occupation: Baker specialising in Turkish baked goods
jobs.description:
Anadolu Bakery on Vollsmose Torv is looking for an experienced baker with expertise in Turkish baked goods. Can you make simit, pide and baklava that keep our customers coming back? Then we would love to hear from you.

About the bakery

Anadolu Bakery is a local bakery in the heart of Vollsmose Torv in Odense. Every day we bake Turkish and Middle Eastern bread and pastries from scratch – for the families, shops and cafés of the neighbourhood. For us, quality, freshness and traditional recipes are everything.

Your tasks

•         Baking Turkish bread such as simit, pide, lavaş and ekmek

•         Making börek, poğaça and other puff pastry and yeast-dough goods

•         Making baklava, kadayıf and other Turkish desserts

•         Planning the daily production so the counter is full from opening time

•         Keeping track of ingredients, hygiene and food safety self-checks

•         Training and supporting colleagues and apprentices in the bakery

What we expect

•         Several years of experience with Turkish baked goods – ideally from Turkey or a Turkish bakery in Denmark

•         That you can work early mornings and weekends

•         That you are reliable and independent, with a firm grip on quality and hygiene

•         That you speak Danish and Turkish

What we offer

•         A permanent full-time position

jobs.occupation: Chief Flight Instructor at GreyBird Pilot Academy - HQ located at Aarhus Airport, DK –  Ready to shape the future of pilot training? ✈️
jobs.description:
GreyBird Pilot Academy is more than a flight school. We are a fast-growing international business in an industry that never stands still – training the next generation of commercial pilots.

Since starting out in Aarhus in 2013, we have grown to seven bases across Europe – from Dublin in the west to Helsinki in the east. Our students fly under the Spanish sun and across European airspace. Today, more than 200 students are training to become commercial pilots with us, supported by over 40 flight instructors and a fleet of 12 Tecnam aircraft, with 13 more on the way.

This is where ambition becomes reality – where safety, people, technology, operations and training must all come together before the wheels leave the runway.

You have an aviation background and have instructed from the cockpit yourself. With us, you will join a highly skilled team with short decision-making lines and plenty of room to shape our development. We turn the dream of flying into a career – and you can help make that journey even better.

The role

The Chief Flight Instructor (CFI) is part of our ATO Core Team and holds overall responsibility for quality, standardisation and compliance in the flight and simulator training delivered by our flight instructors.

You are appointed by the Accountable Manager and report directly to the Head of Training, with whom you work closely to ensure consistent, high-quality training. The Head of Training may delegate tasks and authority to you within your area of responsibility.

Your key responsibilities include:

• 
Standardisation, supervision and training planning for the entire instructor team

• 
Developing and enforcing standard operating procedures for flight training

• 
Ensuring that all instructors hold valid licences, certificates and competencies

• 
Recruiting new instructors as well as guiding, mentoring and providing recurrent training for the existing team

• 
Assessing new bases as we expand into new countries

• 
Updating training materials and operations manuals on our in-house platform, SmartBird

• 
Taking part in ATO and management meetings, where you help set the direction for training

What we offer:

• 
Real decision-making authority over training quality and standards in a growing international organisation

• 
A direct reporting line to the Head of Training and close ties to management

• 
An established ATO with a clear, EASA-approved framework for the role

• 
Access to a modern and growing fleet

• 
An international working environment with colleagues and instructors from several countries

Requirements

The Chief Flight Instructor is a nominated post under EASA Part-ORA (ORA.ATO.210). In line with the regulation, the CFI must hold the highest pilot licence and at least one instructor certificate relevant to the courses the school offers. As GreyBird offers ATPL theory, several aircraft types and type rating-related training, we are looking for:

• 
CPL(A) or ATPL(A)

• 
Instructor certificate: FI(A)

• 
Additional instructor certificates such as CRI(A) and IRI(A) are considered an advantage

• 
A minimum of 1,000 hours as PIC, including at least 500 hours of instructional flying (industry practice is typically 1,500+ hours, and more experience counts in your favour)

• 
Ideally, you also have experience leading, standardising or developing other instructors

• 
Fluent English, spoken and written

How to apply

Ready to set the course for a role where you shape the standards for the next generation of pilots? Send us your application today – we look forward to hearing from you.

jobs.occupation: Postdoc Position: Endocrine Disruption in Fish with Focus on Histopathological Endpoint Development
jobs.description:
We invite applicants for a 3½-years Postdoctoral research position in Environmental Toxicology with a focus on histopathological and behavioral endpoints development in fish. The position is funded by the EU Partnership for Risk Assessment of Chemicals (PARC), the Danish EPA and University of Southern Denmark (SDU). The project will be carried out in the Ecotoxicology group at the Department of Biology, SDU. 

Qualifications: 
The successful candidate must hold a PhD degree in Environmental Toxicology. A strong background in chemical risk and hazard assessment and regulatory toxicology is highly appreciated. This includes knowledge of EU chemicals legislation and regulatory frameworks such as REACH, OECD test guidelines, AOP development, and/or pesticide and biocide risk assessment. Furthermore, the following experiences and skills are required: 

• 
Strong proficiency in English, both written and verbal. 

• 
Experience in teaching and supervision at the university level, including lectures, student examinations, and supervision of MSc students. 

• 
Hands-on experience in assessing endocrine disruption properties of chemicals using the Zebrafish (Danio rerio) model.  

• 
Strong documented knowledge of one or more endocrine pathways relevant to EU regulatory assessments (EATS modalities). 

• 
Extensive experience with OECD fish test protocols such as OECD TG 236 and OECD TG 210. 

• 
Documented experience in histopathology techniques, including tissue preparation, microtome sectioning, cryosectioning, H&E staining, microscopy, and image analysis. 

• 
Experience in behavioral assessment in zebrafish eleutheroembryos, e.g., using EthoVision XT or equivalent tracking and analysis software. 

The following qualifications are considered advantageous: 

• 
Experience with molecular biology techniques, including gene expression analysis (e.g., qPCR, transcriptomics). 

• 
Experience with immunohistochemistry and related imaging techniques. 

This position is particularly suited for a candidate with strong interest in bridging experimental ecotoxicology and regulatory chemical risk- and hazard assessment. 

Application deadline: 13. November 2026 at 23:59 hours local Danish time. 
Please see the full call, including how to apply, on www.sdu.dk

Good decisions start with good data. But good data does not just happen. At NORDEN, data comes from many places and is used across our business to understand markets, automate processes and make better decisions. Your job is to make sure that data is actually ready to be used.

As our new Data Engineer, you will build the pipelines and datasets that move data through our organisation and turn raw information into something people can trust and work with.

You will not be sitting far away from the business maintaining pipelines no one really talks about. You will work closely with digital and commercial colleagues, understand what they need and build the data foundation that helps them solve real problems.

And while shipping knowledge is something you will pick up along the way, curiosity about data and how to make it useful is something we hope you bring from day one.

Why this role?

Because there is a lot to build, improve and figure out.

You will join nine colleagues in our Data Engineering team in Copenhagen, working with large and varied datasets using PySpark, SQL, Azure DevOps and Microsoft Fabric. And our team is growing beyond Copenhagen. We are setting up a Data Engineering team in Singapore, starting with two colleagues, giving you an even broader team to work and share ideas with.

Some days will be about building something new. Others will be about improving what already exists, finding a smarter way to structure data or figuring out why something is not working quite as expected.

What connects it all is the purpose behind it: making data easier to trust, access and use across NORDEN.

You already know your way around data engineering. Now you are looking for a role where you can have more of a say in how things are built, not just build what has already been decided.

You will manage your solutions, contribute to technical decisions and collaborate closely with the business to understand what our data needs to do.

What you will be doing

You will work across the journey from raw data to reliable datasets that colleagues and systems across NORDEN can actually use.

You will:

• Build and maintain scalable data pipelines.

• Bring internal and external data together and turn it into trusted datasets.

• Transform raw data into useful features and insights.

• Improve how we capture, validate and enrich data.

• Build solutions that are reliable today without making life difficult for whoever needs to work with them tomorrow.

• Work with digital and commercial colleagues to understand what they need from our data and translate that into technical solutions.

What you bring

You know that good data solutions are not only about getting things to work, but about making them reliable, scalable and useful to others.

Besides this you likely have:

• A degree within data, IT, engineering or another analytical field.

• Eligibility to work in Denmark.

• Solid experience with Lakehouse architecture, for example in Microsoft Fabric or Azure Databricks.

At NORDEN, our core business applications sit right at the heart of how our commercial teams work. But getting the most out of them is not only about the technology. It is about understanding how shipping actually works, how people use the systems every day and where things could work better.

As our new Business Application Manager, you will bring your shipping experience into that space.

You will work with colleagues across NORDEN to improve how we use our core business applications, optimise the processes around them and help turn business needs into better ways of working.

You do not need to come from IT or have worked as a Business Application Manager before. You understand shipping, likely from operations, control/finance or laytime and are curious about how systems and technology can make the business work better.

Why this role?

Because you get to use your shipping knowledge from a completely new angle.

You will join our Business Applications team of six colleagues across Copenhagen, Cyprus and Singapore, working closely with colleagues from the business as well as Digital Services and Solutions.

Your primary focus will be IMOS, but your work will also take you into applications such as SEDNA, PortLog, Shipfix and other tools used across NORDEN.

Besides this you likely:

• Have worked with shipping business applications and are familiar with IMOS.

Our company

**Our Purpose

**Scheduling isn’t simply filling shifts. It’s finding the sweet spot that enables businesses to grow and team members to enjoy the perfect work/life balance.

At Planday from Xero, we aim to use Agentic AI to build a future where managers seamlessly can free up invaluable time for their business and teams. We’re not just building software; we’re on a mission to make shift work more human, to change work/life balance from a luxury to a reality for all shift workers. We’re using advanced technology to help humans reach their full potential. At work and in life.

Founded in 2004, Planday is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark and helps create perfect schedules for hundreds of thousands of users across the world. Planday was acquired by Xero in 2021.

**How You’ll Make An Impact

**We are introducing customer marketing as a dedicated discipline at Planday, and this is the role that will build it.

This is a builder's role: you will define how we market to our existing customers, establishing the strategy, the programmes, and the ways of working from the ground up. Across the UK, Nordics, and Germany, you will design and deliver 1:many marketing that drives adoption, deepens engagement, and turns customers into long-term advocates and expansion opportunities.

You will sit at the heart of our commercial ambition: as we target growth in the UK, defend our leadership in the Nordics, and build momentum in Germany, customer marketing is one of the key levers that connects product value to commercial outcomes. This is a role for someone who is energised by creating from scratch, earns trust through execution, and knows that the best customer marketing is grounded in deep empathy for the people you are marketing to.

What You'll Do

Establish the Discipline

• Define the customer marketing strategy - audit the current state of customer engagement across all three markets, identify gaps, and build a clear plan for how customer marketing will drive retention, adoption, and expansion at Planday

• Set the operating model - establish the ways of working, tools, segmentation logic, and measurement framework that will underpin everything the function delivers

Lifecycle & Engagement Programmes

Adoption & Expansion

• Lead feature adoption campaigns - work closely with Product Marketing to identify the product features most strongly correlated with retention and satisfaction, and creating targeted campaigns that help customers get more from the platform

• Own upsell and expansion marketing - delivering behaviour-triggered campaigns that move customers up the tiers, support seat growth, and help customers discover the full value of Planday's offering

• Partner with Product Marketing on subscription plan communications and pricing changes, ensuring every customer-facing message reinforces product value and supports commercial goals

Advocacy & Community

• Build Planday's customer advocacy programme - identifying and activating champions within the customer base to generate case studies, reviews, testimonials, and referrals

• Support reference and social proof pipelines across markets - working with Sales, CS, Brand and Regional marketing to ensure high-quality customer stories are available for every stage of the buyer journey

• Explore community-building opportunities - partner with Regional Marketing to execute local community building opportunities such as webinars, customer events, and user groups, that deepen belonging and peer connection among Planday customers

Performance & Insight

• Define and own customer marketing metrics - including engagement rates, adoption scores, NRR contribution, upsell pipeline generated, and advocacy outputs and report regularly against them

• Use customer health data and behavioural signals to identify at-risk segments and inform targeted retention interventions

• Feed customer insight back into the wider marketing and product teams - ensuring the voice of the existing customer shapes how Planday communicates, evolves, and grows

What You'll Bring

**Experience & Skills

**

• 4–6 years in B2B marketing, with clear experience in customer marketing, lifecycle marketing, or retention-focused roles, ideally within a SaaS or technology business

• A track record of building programmes from scratch. You have experience establishing a new discipline, process, or team, not just inheriting and maintaining an existing one

• Multi-market experience, you are comfortable adapting strategy and execution for audiences across different regions, with an understanding of how culture and market maturity shape customer expectations

• Strong lifecycle marketing execution - you know how to design and deliver segmented, behaviour-triggered campaigns across email and in-product channels, and you understand the tools that power them

• Data-led - you use customer health scores, product usage data, and campaign performance metrics to make decisions, not just to report on them

• Experience working cross-functionally with Customer Success, Customer Support, Product, and Sales, you understand the role each function plays in the customer journey and know how to align activity across them

• Familiarity with CRM and marketing automation platforms (e.g. Salesforce, SFMC, HubSpot) and an appetite to make better use of the data and tooling available

How You Show Up

• A builder by nature; you are energised by the blank page, comfortable with ambiguity, and motivated by creating something that didn't exist before

• Commercially grounded; you understand how customer marketing connects to revenue and are comfortable being held to NRR and expansion metrics

• A natural collaborator; you build trust across functions without needing a mandate, and you bring people with you rather than working around them

• Clear and direct communicator; both written and verbal; you can simplify the complex, adapt your message to your audience, and get the room aligned

• AI-curious; you actively explore how AI can improve how you work, from personalisation and segmentation to content creation and performance analysis

Why Planday

At Planday, we firmly believe that diversity and inclusion are the cornerstones of innovation and a vibrant workplace culture. Tasks & Accountabilities

• You will collaborate with our network of external suppliers within the marketing area, maintaining strong relationships and ensuring smooth coordination with external agencies.

• You will work with the Brand Manager and Communication Manager to ensure brand consistency across marketing efforts.

Required Skills

• You have a university degree in marketing (or similar commercial profile)

• You have first working experience in B2B relations

• You have in-depth knowledge of the aircraft after-sales market with a strong sales orientation

• You have demonstrated a track record in creating high-converting marketing content, launching product campaigns, and managing multi-channel promotion strategies.

• You are diplomatic, open-minded with the capability to build successful relations across functions and with all international stakeholders

• You speak English at negotiation level

• You have strong skills in data analytics and data visualization (e.g. Google Analytics) to track and optimize campaign performance.

• You have a great can-do attitude, you see opportunities where others might see challenges

• You are keen to take over transversal projects that are relevant for Satair

What does your next challenge look like?

Healthcare Provider AI Solutions Lead

Ballerup

Your impact begins here

As AI Lead, you will shape how Commercial uses data and AI to work with healthcare providers (HCPs) across all affiliates. You will turn Commercial strategy and Novo’s ambitions into a focused portfolio of AI products and analytics that deliver measurable business outcomes, and you will lead a team of around 10 people to build them. Your work will help leaders make better-informed decisions, today, for people living with serious chronic diseases.

What you’ll bring

You combine hands-on delivery leadership with strong commercial understanding, and you can explain complex AI topics to anyone in the room.

• 
A Master’s degree in Business Management, Computer Science, Statistics, Mathematics or a related field.

• 
10+ years of progressive experience in data, analytics, AI, digital product development or commercial technology roles.

• 
Proven experience leading multidisciplinary teams across data engineering, data science, analytics engineering, product ownership, AI solution development and business analysis, and building capability and high performance.

• 
A strong track record of delivering enterprise-scale AI, machine learning, analytics or decision-support products from idea to production, including adoption, value tracking and continuous improvement.

• 
Deep understanding of commercial business processes and healthcare provider engagement, and the ability to turn strategic priorities into scalable data and AI products.

• 
Experience working with senior business stakeholders and partners across commercial, medical, IT, enterprise architecture, data governance, privacy, legal and operations.

• 
Strength in roadmap management, prioritisation, resource planning, delivery governance and agile ways of working.

• 
A solid understanding of responsible AI, data governance, privacy, security, validation and compliance in a regulated environment.

• 
Excellent communication, influencing and stakeholder management skills.

Useful, but not essential:

• Experience in pharmaceuticals, life sciences, healthcare or another highly regulated industry.

What you’ll do

You will own the Commercial HCP Data & AI roadmap and the team that delivers it, from first idea to a product people use every day.

• 
Shape the roadmap: translate Commercial strategy and Novo’s ambitions into a focused portfolio of AI products and analytics, and set the technical and product direction for reusable data assets, conversational AI, decision-support tools and ML models in line with enterprise architecture, security, platform and data governance standards.

• 
Prioritise what matters: run a pragmatic intake process that balances business value, data readiness, technical feasibility, adoption potential, compliance and team capacity.

• 
Lead and grow your team: manage and develop a multidisciplinary team of approximately 10 people, with clear roles, decision rights and ways of working. Coach on commercial domain knowledge, agile delivery, engineering discipline, data quality, testing, documentation and responsible AI.

• 
Deliver end to end: guide work from opportunity assessment and data readiness through proof of concept, MVP, production, adoption and continuous improvement. Work closely with architects on standards for design, reusable data models, code reviews, testing, model validation, monitoring and support handover.

• 
Track value and reliability: define and monitor business KPIs, adoption, quality and service health, so products keep delivering value after launch.

• 
Embed governance and responsible AI: work with legal, privacy, IT security and risk to ensure trusted data sources, clear ownership, access controls, lineage, GDPR compliance, transparency and human oversight.

Who you’ll work with

You will lead a multidisciplinary team in Enterprise IT & Quality, where colleagues work across the Novo value chain, stay close to stakeholders and help deliver trusted technology, high quality and responsible ways of working.

You will be the bridge between Commercial and technology. Your closest partners will be Commercial business teams and product owners, along with enterprise architecture, platform teams, data governance, privacy, legal and operations. You will also work with senior business leaders and affiliates, turning Commercial opportunities into clear problem statements, solution options and delivery plans that technical and non-technical colleagues can act on.

Together, you will remove blockers, create clarity on priorities and embed new tools in daily decision-making.

What you can expect here

Data and AI are strategic priorities at Novo, and you will have strong leadership sponsorship for this work. You will influence Commercial strategy, partner with senior executives and help define how AI changes decision-making in a rapidly evolving pharmaceutical landscape.

You will be trusted to take ownership and be supported to perform at your best, in a culture that values curiosity and innovation. You will grow your leadership and technology career by leading a talented team, working across functions and building new skills along the way.

For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from 940,800.00 to 1,448,700.00 DKK, corresponding to the level of the position.
